Box Office Progress and Milestones

The fantasy drama Mookuthi Amman 2 has officially crossed the Rs 20 crore mark in India net earnings during its theatrical run. Despite achieving this notable financial milestone, the feature is encountering difficulties in sustaining the strong momentum established during its opening week.

On its tenth day in theaters, the movie brought in Rs 84 lakh in India net revenue. This latest single-day addition pushes the film's cumulative domestic net total to Rs 20.09 crore, while the corresponding India gross collection has reached Rs 23.22 crore across various territories.

Second Week Slowdown and Daily Trends

Following a robust debut week that yielded Rs 17.93 crore in domestic net collections, the picture has experienced a marked cooling in its daily ticket sales. The sequential drop highlights a significant shift as the project moves further into its theatrical schedule.

Specifically, the earnings for the three-day stretch covering days eight through ten added a modest Rs 2.16 crore to the domestic ledger. The domestic gross for this same weekend phase stands at Rs 2.50 crore, supported by a total count of 14,487 shows recorded over its ten-day run.

Sunday Collection Comparison

Data compiled by Sacnilk indicates that the feature collected Rs 84 lakh on Sunday, November 15. This figure represents a slight 1.2% decline compared to the previous day's collection of Rs 85 lakh on Saturday.

Although the drop from Saturday to Sunday is minimal, it underscores a plateau in audience footfall as word of mouth and initial excitement transition into steady, lower-volume weekday and weekend trends.

Strong Box Office Performance

The mythological feature continues to draw heavy crowds to theatres across the nation. Even as the film enters its second week of exhibition, audience turnout remains exceptionally high, keeping ticket counters busy.

The Hindi version of the movie has consistently maintained the top position, while dubbed versions in various regional languages have significantly bolstered the pan-India box office numbers.

Day 12 Earnings Breakdown

On its twelfth day in cinemas, tracking data indicates that the feature pulled in Rs 32 crore net across India. This total was accumulated from a vast deployment of 22,365 shows nationwide.

The Hindi language screenings generated the lion's share with Rs 23.75 crore from 17,742 shows. Meanwhile, regional markets also delivered notable contributions to the daily tally.

Regional Language Contributions

Malayalam screenings brought in Rs 2.85 crore utilizing 1,061 shows, while Kannada language showings secured Rs 2 crore across 892 screenings.

Further augmenting the totals, Tamil language runs collected Rs 1.90 crore from 1,158 shows, and Telugu screenings contributed Rs 1.50 crore from 1,512 shows.

Overall Totals and Milestones

Although the daily revenue experienced a 57.3 percent drop compared to the eleventh day, the collective financial run remains remarkably robust.

With these latest additions, the total domestic net collection for the feature has reached Rs 792.60 crore, placing it firmly on the verge of the monumental Rs 800 crore threshold.

Cast and Creative Team

The project is spearheaded by Ranbir Kapoor portraying Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi playing Sita, and Yash appearing as Ravana. The narrative draws inspiration from multiple historical versions, including the Valmiki Ramayana.

The film was directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who additionally co-wrote the screenplay alongside Shridhar Raghavan. Production duties were managed by Namit Malhotra and Yash.

Ensemble Supporting Cast and Sequels

Alongside the primary leads, the extensive ensemble cast features Ravie Dubey, Addinath Kothare, Lara Dutta, Vivek Oberoi, Rakul Preet Singh, Indira Krishnan, and Arun Govil.

Makers have already established plans for a follow-up project, with a sequel slated for a theatrical release in 2028 that will incorporate Sunny Deol as Lord Hanuman.

Festival Screening Honor

Beyond commercial milestones, the cinematic piece has been selected to open the BRICS segment at the upcoming 57th International Film Festival of India hosted in Goa.

Set to commence on November 20, the festival segment aims to present international cinematic traditions from all eleven BRICS member nations alongside various partner countries.

ld.articleBody:
A Major Partnership Announcement

Renowned composer A.R. Rahman has officially been named the brand ambassador for Brooke Bond Taj Mahal Tea. The prominent beverage label falls under the corporate umbrella of Hindustan Unilever Limited.

This new collaboration establishes a significant chapter in the beverage company's lengthy history of intertwining its brand identity with musical artistry.

The Awaken Your Masterpiece Campaign

In tandem with his appointment, the Oscar and Grammy-winning artist has launched an advertising initiative titled 'Awaken Your Masterpiece'. The central theme of the campaign revolves around the importance of creativity, dedication, and artistic excellence.

The newly released promotional film features the celebrated musician navigating a creative block. He pauses his work to enjoy a freshly brewed cup of the beverage, which helps him regain his inspiration and finish an uplifting melody.

Celebrating Craftsmanship and Finesse

For more than six decades, the tea brand has cultivated an identity centered on fine craftsmanship. It frequently uses signature phrases like 'Hazaaron Mein Ek' and 'Wah Taj!' to communicate its premium market positioning.

The inclusion of the legendary composer draws direct creative parallels. The brand emphasizes that just as the musician's work is born from finding the exact right note among infinite possibilities, every single cup uses leaves chosen from thousands to achieve a distinct taste.

Corporate and Creative Perspectives

Ishtpreet Singh, who serves as the Vice President of Beverages at Hindustan Unilever Limited, shared thoughts on the partnership. He noted that music and the tea label have remained inseparable for decades, beginning with previous associations alongside legendary figures.

He expressed that no better custodian could carry the legacy forward than an artist whose creative genius is genuinely rare and distinct.

Vision From the Creative Team

The creative direction for the project was guided by Ogilvy India leadership, including Harshad Rajadhyaksha and Kainaz Karmakar. They highlighted the continuous journey of establishing a brand deeply rooted in musical foundations.

Additionally, the promotional spot was brought to life by filmmaker Prakash Varma of Nirvana Films, an individual who has helped shape the visual aesthetics of the product line for more than ten years.

Carrying Forward a Legendary Musical Legacy

This fresh collaboration extends a long tradition of musical partnerships for the product line. In previous years, the brand famously collaborated with tabla maestro Ustad Zakir Hussain.

By bringing the iconic composer on board, the latest initiative aims to build upon that historical foundation by celebrating ongoing artistic achievements and the pursuit of mastery.

Availability Across Platforms

The newly minted promotional video has officially made its debut. Consumers and fans can view the content across multiple digital and marketing channels tied to the brand.
